app_record_conflict.description: Wire 3.2 Equal times, spec 4.2: two records of alice's wallet, signed with its signing key, with the same updated_at and different bodies (the board kinds in their tasks member, protocols.tasks). Both verify; together they are a conflict for every reader, which uses neither and keeps the earlier record it holds, here the wallet app record of documents, until a record with a later updated_at. The switch refuses the second of them (the app_put steps of claims.json).

accepted.name: the member of a protocol no reader here knows: other

app_record_protocols.description: Wire 3.2 Protocols' members: the form of an app record's protocols, on documents.json's wallet app record with one member added beside the tasks member (or, last of refused, protocols itself replaced), signed again with the wallet's signing key. protocols is an object; each name has the syntax of a scope name, 1 to 32 characters of a-z, 0-9, _ and -, starting with a letter or digit; each value is an object, or null, which is no member. refused are records every reader refuses, the switch included; accepted are ones every reader takes, ignoring the member of a protocol it doesn't know, and a tasks reader reads the tasks member as before. protocols is the record's protocols member as signed. reason is the prototype's wording.

refused.name: a protocol name with a dot: my.tasks
a member that is an array
refused.reason: invalid: the member of protocol other isn't an object

refused.name: a member that is a string
refused.reason: invalid: the member of protocol other isn't an object

refused.name: a member that is a number
refused.reason: invalid: the member of protocol other isn't an object

refused.name: protocols that isn't an object
refused.reason: invalid: json: a member has the wrong type or value at line 1 column 1092

approval.description: Wire 3.10: the wallet's approval, the companion claim of its grant approval: the hash of its app request, its certificate, alice's identity.json version 3 listing it, and its full key bundle (data epochs 1 and 2 and the naming key), one part sealed with fixed randomness (seeds approval/cek, approval/nonce, approval/ikm-e) to its bundle key and signed by alice's identity key. It holds no key in the clear.

rejections.name: a part through data epoch 3, at data epoch 2
rejections.rule: an approval's key bundle parts cover every data epoch from 1 to its identity.json's data_epoch and none goes past it, since at approval there is no next epoch (wire 3.5, 3.10 step 4)

auth_request.description: Wire 3.9: the Pubky auth request the wallet's app request binds: its secret (only its hash is in the request), client ID, client key and capabilities.

description: Signed documents (wire 2.2, 3): carried as { "body": base64url of the exact JSON bytes, "sig": base64url }, in headers as "<body>.<sig>". Signed document bytes are lp(body bytes, signature); every hash over a document (certificate hashes in identity.json, chain item hashes, the freeze hash) is BLAKE3 of those bytes. Each identity.json names its signing install in signer, a 16-byte signer ID (seeds alice/signer and bob/signer).

discarded.description: Wire 3.6: the next service's signed answer that it discarded the import bound to the freeze, with the service key the freeze names (seed service/alice/next), and the unfreeze as the signer then sends it to the old service.

identity_rejections.description: Wire 3.3: identity.json documents every reader refuses, the switch included. Each is alice's identity.json version 3 with one member of its body text changed, signed again by her identity key, so its signature verifies and only the document's rules refuse it. error is the core's wording.

cases.name: duplicate: claims.read twice
cases.reason: invalid: permissions: not each once in the fixed order

cases.name: reordered: claims.write before claims.read
cases.reason: invalid: permissions: not each once in the fixed order

cases.reason: invalid: permissions: "claims.admin" isn't a switch permission

permission_rejections.description: Wire 3.1: certificates every verifier refuses, the switch included, for a permissions list that isn't well formed: a name that isn't a switch permission, a name twice, or names out of the fixed order. Each is the wallet certificate of documents with permissions changed, signed by alice's identity key; the signatures verify. reason is the prototype's wording at the switch.

accepted.name: a sub-scope of a name no protocol here defines: future:a

scope_rule.description: Wire 3.1: the switch's scope rule, on documents.json's wallet certificate (scopes tasks, tasks_people, tasks_people_admin) with scopes added and its permissions kept, signed by alice's identity key. A scope is name or name:<sub>: a name is 1 to 32 characters of a-z, 0-9, _ and -, starting with a letter or digit, and a sub has the syntax of a label; each once, never a name beside one of its name:<sub>, at most 32 in all. refused are certificates every verifier refuses, the switch included; accepted are ones the switch takes, and every other verifier too, ignoring the names it doesn't know. reason is the prototype's wording.

refused.name: a name in upper case: Tasks
refused.reason: invalid: "Tasks" isn't a scope name or name:<sub>

refused.name: an empty name: :x
refused.reason: invalid: ":x" isn't a scope name or name:<sub>

refused.name: a sub-scope with a dot: future:a.b
refused.reason: invalid: "future:a.b" isn't a scope name or name:<sub>

refused.name: a sub-scope beside its parent: tasks_people and tasks_people:a
refused.reason: invalid: tasks_people and tasks_people:a together: tasks_people covers every tasks_people:<sub>
